meta.scene_summary: We are building the future with one hand while the other desperately tries to unplug the infrastructure.

cooking.headline: The government is trying to unplug the neighborhood watch.
cooking.summary: Senators are pushing to ban automated license plate readers that turn every suburban street into a surveillance grid. It turns out people are starting to realize that 'smart neighborhood' is just a fancy marketing term for a private police state.

cooking.headline: Pop!_OS is allergic to AI code, and honestly, I get it.
cooking.summary: System76 is banning AI-generated code from their codebase because they'd rather debug their own mistakes than spend all day untangling a hallucinated mess. It's the software equivalent of a professor demanding you show your work instead of just handing in a generated essay.
cooking.plain_english: The developers of the Linux distribution Pop!_OS have prohibited the use of AI-generated code in their primary software projects to ensure code quality and maintainability.

cooking.headline: Rust builds just got a speed boost, finally giving us time to stare at the wall
cooking.summary: By emitting metadata earlier in the process, Rust builds are now twice as fast, which is great news for anyone whose entire personality is waiting for a compiler. Now you can get back to your code twice as fast only to realize you still have no idea why it is broken.
cooking.plain_english: A change in how the Rust compiler handles metadata allows the software building process to complete up to two times faster.

cooking.headline: Yann LeCun thinks AI extinction fears are just a group project gone wrong
cooking.summary: Yann LeCun is publicly dismissing existential AI risks while other leaders are busy building their own bunkers. It turns out that when you build the tech, you're the one who thinks the group project is definitely not going to spontaneously combust.
cooking.plain_english: Yann LeCun has publicly stated that he does not believe artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to humanity.

cooking.headline: Distributed energy is the ultimate 'serverless' architecture for survival
cooking.summary: Ukraine is keeping the lights on by moving from a few giant power plants to thousands of smaller, scattered energy sources. It turns out that decentralizing your infrastructure is a lot harder for an attacker to take down than a single, monolithic data center.
cooking.plain_english: Ukraine has successfully maintained its power grid during the war by transitioning to a network of many small, distributed renewable energy sources instead of relying on a few large power plants.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's safety lead just left the group project.
cooked.summary: The person responsible for keeping the AI from going rogue quit because the company's internal culture is allegedly a mess. It turns out that building god-like intelligence is slightly harder when your team is having a mid-life crisis.
cooked.plain_english: A senior official in charge of AI safety has resigned from OpenAI, citing concerns about the company's internal culture and priorities.

cooked.headline: A federal judge just told Flock that 'mass surveillance' isn't a feature, it's a bug.
cooked.summary: Flock marketed their cameras as a neighborhood watch upgrade, but a federal judge just ruled that tracking everyone everywhere is actually just indiscriminate mass surveillance. It turns out that 'safety' is a hard sell when you're technically acting like a panopticon with a subscription model.
cooked.plain_english: A federal judge ruled that the company Flock's automated license plate recognition technology constitutes indiscriminate mass surveillance.

cooked.headline: OpenBSD devs look at Rust-based coreutils and say 'no thanks'
cooked.summary: OpenBSD developers rejected a Rust-based rewrite of standard tools because they prefer their code to be as old and grumpy as they are. It turns out that when you prioritize security and stability, 'rewritten in Rust' is not the magic spell you think it is.
cooked.plain_english: OpenBSD has decided not to adopt a new set of system tools written in the Rust programming language due to concerns about licensing and compatibility.

cooked.headline: Sam Altman's family drama just got a permanent 'Access Denied' from the courts.
cooked.summary: After a legal back-and-forth, the judge finally dismissed the lawsuit brought by Sam Altman's sister. It turns out that even with the world's most powerful AI, some family problems are better solved by a court clerk hitting the delete key.
cooked.plain_english: A lawsuit filed by Sam Altman's sister against him regarding sexual abuse allegations has been dismissed by a judge.

cooked.headline: The iPhone 18 Pro Max is now a very expensive paperweight if you use AT&T.
cooked.summary: Apple has officially confirmed that certain iPhone 18 Pro Max units are incompatible with AT&T and require a total hardware swap. It's the ultimate 'it's not you, it's me' breakup, except you have to go to the Apple Store to get your divorce papers.
cooked.plain_english: Apple has acknowledged that some iPhone 18 Pro Max models are experiencing connectivity issues with AT&T's network and must be replaced.
